item.text:
**Bottom Line**

Mostly negative. Tshisekedi did follow through on some formal commitments in 2024, especially around coalition formation, IMF-backed fiscal reform, anti-corruption oversight, and peace-process diplomacy. But the year also shows repeated reversals and evasions: term-limit talk shifted toward third-term risk, peace commitments were not durable, public narratives about security and governance were often at odds with conditions on the ground, and repression of journalists and activists undercut honest disclosure of tradeoffs.

**Accepted Claims**

- `DR Congo president names planning minister as new PM` | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/dr-congo-president-names-planning-minister-as-new-pm/2023882/) | Tshisekedi’s appointment of Judith Suminwa ended weeks of coalition uncertainty after his inauguration. This is limited positive evidence that he did honor the formal coalition-building process before forming a government. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.5, 7B.6

- `DRC: 2024 Article IV Consultation, Sixth Review...` | IMF | 2024-07-03 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr) | The IMF says the authorities kept prudent macro policies, improved revenue mobilization, and used corrective measures when targets slipped. This is moderate evidence that the administration followed through on at least part of its stabilization commitments. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.4, 7B.6, 7B.5

- `DRC reaches agreement on ECF and RSF arrangements` | IMF | 2024-11-13 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf) | The new IMF package was explicitly framed around governance, transparency, tighter spending-chain controls, and anti-capture reforms. That supports some evidence of keeping fiscal reform commitments, though implementation remained limited. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.4, 7B.6, 7B.5

- `Le Chef de l’État a assisté à l’ouverture de la session extraordinaire du conseil supérieur de la Cour des comptes` | Présidence RDC | 2024-10-07 | [URL](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes) | Tshisekedi publicly backed the Court of Accounts’ oversight function, and the court said his support helped revive public-finance control. This is positive evidence that he sometimes reinforced rather than undermined formal accountability commitments. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.6, 7B.7

- `DR Congo: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis` | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty says Tshisekedi made numerous human-rights pledges in his first term but little to no progress followed, and it highlights squandered public resources and underfunded services. This is strong negative evidence for keeping promises and acknowledging tradeoffs honestly. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.2, 7B.7, 7B.6

- `DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations` | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/) | Amnesty says Tshisekedi ignored worsening human-rights conditions while the state of siege and crackdown on dissent deepened. The report portrays the government as using public messaging to conceal coercive tradeoffs rather than confronting them. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.2, 7B.7, 7B.6

- `East and Southern Africa: Journalists targeted amid ongoing crackdown on media` | Amnesty International | 2024-05-03 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/media-freedom-under-threat/) | Amnesty reports authorities closed a dozen media outlets and programs on accusations like false rumors and revolt. This is direct evidence that the government manipulated public information and punished scrutiny rather than respecting open disclosure. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2

- `DR Congo: Authorities must immediately free detained journalist` | Amnesty International | 2024-03-08 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-authorities-must-immediately-free-detained-journalist/) | Amnesty says Stanis Bujakera’s detention was judicial harassment meant to chill criticism. That is strong evidence of punishing truth-tellers, which cuts directly against promise-keeping and honest public accounting. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.2

- `Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts - report` | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/) | Reuters reports a civil-society finding that CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. That is strong evidence of concealed tradeoffs and non-transparent handling of a core public process. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.6, 7B.4, 7B.7

- `Congo President Tshisekedi draws criticism over constitutional reform plans` | Reuters | 2024-10-24 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-154945419.html) | Reuters says Tshisekedi created a commission to study constitutional revisions that could remove term limits and allow a third term. That is the clearest 2024 example of opportunistic reversal on a formal commitment. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.1, 7B.2, 7B.6

- `Congo and Rwanda say peace talks in Angola will not take place` | Reuters | 2024-12-15 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/congo-rwanda-peace-talks-angola-130008004.html) | The planned Angola summit collapsed after deadlock over direct DRC-M23 dialogue. Tshisekedi kept using diplomacy, but the late-year failure weakens any strong claim that his peace commitments produced durable results. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.1, 7B.6

- `DR Congo President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations` | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/) | Amnesty says the government failed to ensure transparent investigation and accountability after Makala prison deaths and sexual violence. This is negative evidence that the administration concealed or downplayed failures instead of owning them. | IDs: 7B.8; also 7B.7, 7B.6

**Search Gap**

- I found no clean, comprehensive promise ledger for Tshisekedi in 2024.
- The strongest evidence is indirect: formal commitments on coalition formation, peace talks, fiscal reform, and oversight were sometimes followed, but the public record also shows major reversals, selective disclosure, and suppression of scrutiny.
- On balance, the year looks more like partial follow-through under heavy political pressure than consistent promise-keeping.
